pregunta: You ___ pay to enter the museum. It's free!
respuesta: You **don't have to** pay to enter the museum. It's free!

pregunta: You ___ park here. It's a fire exit.
respuesta: You **mustn't** park here. It's a fire exit.

pregunta: He's been yawning all evening. He ___ be tired.
respuesta: He's been yawning all evening. He **must** be tired.

pregunta: She ___ be at work. I've just seen her at the gym.
respuesta: She **can't** be at work. I've just seen her at the gym.

pregunta: When I was young, I ___ run ten kilometres without stopping.
respuesta: When I was young, I **could** run ten kilometres without stopping.

pregunta: After three hours, I finally ___ fix my bike.
respuesta: After three hours, I finally **was able to** fix my bike.
explicacion: Para un logro concreto en el pasado se usa **was able to** (o **managed to**), no could.

pregunta: You ___ see a dentist about that tooth.
respuesta: You **should** see a dentist about that tooth.

pregunta: I ___ go out tonight, but I'm not sure yet.
respuesta: I **might** go out tonight, but I'm not sure yet.

pregunta: We ___ wear a uniform at my school. It's the rule.
respuesta: We **have to** wear a uniform at my school. It's the rule.
explicacion: Es una norma (obligación), no un consejo.

pregunta: I hope I'll ___ come to your wedding.
respuesta: I hope I'll **be able to** come to your wedding.
explicacion: Después de **will** no puede ir can.

pregunta: You ___ have told me! I would have helped you.
respuesta: You **should** have told me! I would have helped you.
explicacion: Reproche: «deberías habérmelo dicho». **must have** sería una deducción.

pregunta: I can't find my keys. I ___ have left them at the office.
respuesta: I can't find my keys. I **must** have left them at the office.

pregunta: You ___ use a pen. A pencil is fine too.
respuesta: You **don't have to** use a pen. A pencil is fine too.
